 November 30, 2015.  BOF was sold to the Farmers & Merchants Bank in Stuttgart, Arkansas ("F&M") on November 30, 2015.  F&M paid cash in exchange for
 all of BOF's outstanding shares of common stock.  Consequently, all of our holdings in BOF stock were liquidated to cash as a result of BOF's sale.  This affected
 our investment holdings in two ways.  First, my wife held BOF stock in her 401-K account (see Line 2).  Secondly, my wife and I jointly held BOF stock in the
 name of TLB & MBB Family Investments, LLC ("TLB&MBB") (see Line 8).  The cash proceeds from TLB&MBB's BOF stock sale was then deposited into a
 new investment account at Wells Fargo (see Line 10).  
2.  Part VII, Lines 1 - 7, and 11.  My wife's employment terminated in conjunction with the closing of the sale of BOF, as explained in the preceding paragraph. 
 Consequently, my wife's 401-K account was terminated as well.  This resulted in the liquidation of the stock and mutual funds held in her 401-K (see Lines 1 - 7),
 the cash proceeds of which were rolled over into an IRA account at Wells Fargo (see Line 11).

1. Part VIL Upon confirmation, | sold my partnership interest in my law firm (Taylor Law Partners, LLP), and the entity that owned the law firm's building

(Sanity, LLC). 1also liquidated my 401K account, which held the mutual funds noted as being sold,

2. Part VIL. [J cxcrcised employment related stock options which, for tax purposes, was treated as W-2 income.

On June 6, 2017, the Committee sent a letter inquiry regarding my listing of "Arvest Bank Deposit Accounts” on my 2016 report. The letter explamed that "[1}f

this account was opened during the reporting period, the information required in Columns D(1)-(3) should have been provided.” For clarification, my wife and

1 did open Arvest deposit accounts during 2016. The source of those deposits was my wife's severance income (paid in 2016) when she ended her employment

contract (at the end of 2015) with a previous employer. For tax purposes this was treated as personal income to my wife,

Additionally, in June 2016 we sold our home. The equity proceeds from that sale were deposited into the Arvest deposit accounts. In July 2016 we purchased a lot

and began building a new house --- using the equity proceeds from our old house (that were deposited into the Arvest accounts) during the building process -- that

occurred during 2016 and 2017.

In Section VII, Line 1, an “investment” is listed called "TLB & MBB Family Investments, LLC." The audit report for the financial disclosure report shows an error

here --- presumably because there is no "income" reported for this entry. This LLC is the vehicle through which my wife and | own an interest in an old family

farm. The property is being held long term. There is no income associated with this LLC.
